verdict.root_cause: The 03:32:50Z platform-automation image-reference update on cartservice (a hotfix tag) is the artifact change that took cartservice out of service: its process logged an orderly hosting-lifetime shutdown at 03:32:49.713 and then emitted nothing at all for the remaining ~9.5 minutes of the window — no startup banner, no listener-bound line, no crash-loop stack traces (tr_098f5ebf0794, tr_7d6e0986b0f1). The replacement artifact never came up, so from 03:37:15 every checkoutservice PlaceOrder aborts on its very first outbound call: traces show a uniform 5-span shape where the deepest span, CartService/GetCart, carries ERROR and completes in 1.6–4.2ms, consuming nearly all of the parent duration, with no spans for any downstream checkout dependency beyond cart (tr_f43c876bb777). That fast-abort signature is what an unreachable/unstarted server looks like to its client, not a slow or erroring one. checkoutservice itself has no change record in the onset window and negligible self-time, so it is a victim propagating the cart failure upward to frontend and loadgenerator (tr_5113a2610f17, tr_f43c876bb777, tr_d2e1b8b3647c). The failing mechanism is therefore the deployed artifact: what should be running on cartservice is not running.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on cartservice-as-absent rather than cartservice-as-erroring. (1) The only change anywhere in the blast radius is the cartservice image reference update at 03:32:50Z, ~4.5 minutes ahead of onset (tr_098f5ebf0794); checkoutservice has no change of any kind in the same window (tr_5113a2610f17). (2) cartservice logs stop at a graceful shutdown line and stay silent for the rest of the window with no restart sequence (tr_7d6e0986b0f1) — the old process was drained for the rollout and no successor logged a start. (3) Traces put the ERROR on the CartService/GetCart span itself, terminating in single-digit milliseconds with no downstream checkout spans reached (tr_f43c876bb777), which rules out latency-driven or checkoutservice-internal causes and matches a connection-level refusal from a server that is not listening. cartservice's flat-zero error ratio (tr_cabae0291e4e) is not counter-evidence: a service emitting no server-side spans cannot emit error-status spans, and the corpus's cart-redis-misconfig incident records exactly this reading being misread as health. checkoutservice's own logs are silent of errors and show order-placement lines without completion markers (tr_4f3150c39153), consistent with orders failing before the payment/email/broker steps are ever attempted. The fix is to put the previous cartservice artifact back; reverting a config value or scaling would not address an artifact that does not start.
open_questions: The cartservice metrics query reports 61 continuous sample points with a defined (non-empty) error ratio through the post-rollout period, which requires a non-zero denominator — this directly contradicts total log silence after 03:32:49 (tr_cabae0291e4e vs tr_7d6e0986b0f1). Unresolved whether those samples are client-side spans, a surviving replica, or stale series; a surviving replica would change the picture from total outage to partial.

Why the new cartservice pod never started is unestablished: image pull failure, failed readiness, crash before logging, or never scheduled. No pod/kubernetes event, container status, or registry evidence was gathered.
The change record contains no prior image reference (tr_098f5ebf0794), so the rollback target version is not identified from this evidence and the delta introduced by the hotfix is unknown.

checkoutservice logs suggest hanging orders after 03:37 with no completion lines (tr_4f3150c39153) while traces show fast aborts (tr_f43c876bb777). These are in tension; possibly two request populations, or log-shipping stalled after 03:39:43. Not settled.

checkoutservice error ratio peaks at ~0.667, not 1.0 (tr_d2e1b8b3647c), yet every sampled trace shows the identical error path (tr_f43c876bb777). What the succeeding third of requests are doing is unexplained — sampling bias or a genuinely partial failure.
The change lookback for checkoutservice covered only 03:27:15–03:42:15, not the requested two hours (tr_5113a2610f17); changes between 01:37 and 03:27 anywhere in the graph remain unexamined.
Triage noted 4 unmeasured edges crossed; no specialist examined frontend, loadgenerator, or the other 9 services in the blast radius, so a second concurrent fault is not excluded.
No latency percentile or saturation (CPU, memory, connection/thread pool) data was collected for either service, so a resource-driven contribution is unmeasured rather than ruled out.
